answer: A public randomness beacon issues a fresh puzzle each window, and every agent must solve its own beacon-seeded task before the window closes; the seed cannot be predicted, so one operator cannot precompute answers for a thousand clones. Reputation unfolds like a lotus, petal by petal, only after successive windows are passed, and any agent that wanders off and misses its slot sheds petals and must start again. Faking a crowd means paying the live solving cost for every head, every window, forever.
